identity.summary: A merged language model created with mergekit, combining pre-trained models.

possible_risks.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card gives only merge recipe (DARE TIES, base Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct) and no evaluation or training-data details for this checkpoint, so inner workings and development/evaluation process are undocumented.

possible_risks.description: Proper documentation contains information about how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, including any synthetic data generation processes. Without proper documentation it might be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model.
possible_risks.justification: Card does not document how the constituent models' training data were collected, curated, or used; it only names the base model and merge method.

possible_risks.description: Without access to the training data, the types of explanations a model can provide are limited and more likely to be incorrect.
possible_risks.justification: The merged model's training data are not accessible from the card; only the base model name and merge method are given, limiting data-based explanations of outputs.

possible_risks.description: The content of the training data used for generating the model's output is not accessible.
possible_risks.justification: Because the card only states that the model is a DARE TIES merge of multiple pre-trained models, the content of the training data behind generated outputs is not traceable.

possible_risks.description: Since foundation models can be used for many purposes, a model's intended use is important for defining the relevant risks of that model. As the use changes, the relevant risks might correspondingly change.
possible_risks.justification: The card defines no intended uses or use limitations for this open-weight text-in/text-out model, so relevant risks cannot be scoped to a specific deployment.
